---
title: "Overview and detail"
description: "Bind one panel's view to a brush on another with bind_scale(). Drag a range on the overview strip and the detail panel pans and zooms to match."
categories: [Interactive]
image: figs/overview-detail.png
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_helper.R")
library(vellumwidget)

set.seed(1)
n <- 400L
walk <- data.frame(
  t  = seq.Date(as.Date("2021-01-01"), by = "day", length.out = n),
  id = seq_len(n)
)
walk$v <- cumsum(rnorm(n, sd = 1.1))

# Static preview for the gallery card: the detail line on its own.
prev <- vplot(walk) |>
  mark_line(x = t, y = v, color = "#6b4f2c")
render_plot(prev, "figs/overview-detail.png", dpi = 150)
```

`bind_scale()` ties one panel's axis to an interval selection declared on
another. Brush a range on an overview plot and the detail plot pans and zooms to
that range. The view moves without a re-render or a scale retrain, so a long
series stays legible: keep the whole shape in a thin strip, read the part you
care about up close.

This is the third thing a selection can drive, alongside the spotlight and
cross-filter of the [declarative interactivity](declarative-interactivity.qmd)
entry. Here the gesture changes what a panel shows rather than how it is styled.

## A daily series, four hundred points long

The overview draws the full random walk. `select_interval(on = "x")` gives it an
x-only brush, and `add_selection()` attaches that brush to the overview's marks.
The detail draws the same series and calls `bind_scale()` on the brush, binding
its x-axis to the selected range. Drag a window on the lower strip and the upper
panel zooms into it.

```{r}
range <- select_interval("range", on = "x")

detail <- vplot(walk) |>
  mark_line(x = t, y = v, data_id = id) |>
  bind_scale(range, aes = "x") |>
  labs(title = "Detail — follows the brush below", x = NULL, y = "value")

overview <- vplot(walk) |>
  mark_line(x = t, y = v) |>
  add_selection(range) |>
  labs(title = "Overview — brush a range", x = NULL, y = NULL)

concat(
  detail, overview,
  design = "
    A
    A
    B
  "
) |>
  as_widget(height = 480)
```

The strip below stays put while you read the panel above, and the brush window
tracks the detail view both ways: zoom the detail with the wheel or the keyboard
and the window on the overview resizes to match. An empty brush leaves the detail
at its full range, so the plot opens showing everything.
